label: Modelled from 2024 BACI trade, benchmarked against EIA. Not a published statistic.
assumptions: Representative ports and shortest maritime paths approximate routes. A fallback is a geographic mainland proxy. A shipment may use a different port or passage.
The combined measure uses 42.3 GJ/t for crude oil, 43 for refined products, 50 for LNG and 24 for coal. These are draft average heating values. Pipeline gas is reported separately.
The draft minor importer floor is 10 PJ per year.

Measured port allocations balance national terminal shares with destination tonnage. Their draft weights decrease exponentially with sea distance (one e-fold per 1000 km). Route lines show the largest modelled port pair for the product.
HS 271121 pipeline gas is land-only and kept separate from LNG.
Trade with an unresolved route is included in all imports. Only routes assigned to sea enter the seaborne denominator.
All product shares use tonnes. Missing quantities and quantities priced below one third of the tonne-weighted HS6 median are estimated from declared trade value at that median price.
Declared partners include re-exports. An EIA-documented China crude origin correction affects routing only. The HS product groups are coarse.
Routes describe a baseline, before modelling Red Sea diversions. EIA counts observed transit, including routes and product scopes this model approximates.
IMF PortWatch live traffic is gated pending permission and is not an input to these structural shares.

sourceOverride.note: EIA Figure 8 estimates Iran supplied 11% of Chinese crude oil and condensate in 2024. EIA identifies Iranian crude relabeling as a material source of China’s declared Malaysia imports. Use that rounded share against the screened HS 2709 China total, subtract already-declared Iran tonnes, then cap at the screened Malaysia flow. This allocates routing only; it preserves the declared supplier, original BACI quantity and model import denominators. No attribution is made outside this product, trade pair and year. The available Malaysia bucket may be smaller than the EIA-implied misattribution, and the source provides no parcel-level match.
